hints: Focus on what a multiple bond really contains, as every single, double and triple bond has exactly one sigma bond.
Expand the condensed formula to see all the atoms, there is one H on the left alkyne, one H on the right alkene, plus two CH3 groups.
Add the sigma bonds along the carbon skeleton to the nine C-H sigma bonds to get the total count.
walkthrough:
**Recall the sigma rule for multiple bonds**

Every single bond is one $\sigma$ bond. A double bond is one $\sigma$ plus one $\pi$, and a triple bond is one $\sigma$ plus two $\pi$.

So for counting $\sigma$, count 1 for every bond line connection, whether single, double or triple.

**Draw out the skeleton**

Write the molecule as $\text{H}-\text{C}_1\equiv\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3(\text{CH}_3)=\text{C}_4(\text{H})(\text{CH}_3)$.

Skeleton $\sigma$ bonds are: $\text{H}-\text{C}_1$ (1), $\text{C}_1\equiv\text{C}_2$ (1), $\text{C}_2-\text{C}_3$ (1), $\text{C}_3-\text{CH}_3$ (1), $\text{C}_3=\text{C}_4$ (1), $\text{C}_4-\text{H}$ (1), $\text{C}_4-\text{CH}_3$ (1). That is 7 $\sigma$ bonds.

**Count the C-H bonds in the methyl groups**

Each $\text{CH}_3$ has 3 $\text{C}-\text{H}$ single bonds, and each single bond is a $\sigma$ bond.

$$2 \times 3 = 6 \text{ } \sigma \text{ bonds in methyl groups}$$

**Add everything together**

Total $\sigma$ = skeleton $\sigma$ + methyl $\sigma$.

$$7 + 6 = 13 \text{ } \sigma \text{ bonds}$$

options.A: Too small. This counts only about 5 bonds, perhaps only the C-C backbone or only the pi bonds. It misses that every C-H single bond is also a sigma bond, and there are 9 of those alone.
options.B: Too low by 2. This usually comes from forgetting some hydrogens when the formula is condensed, for example counting only one CH3 group fully or missing the alkyne H and alkene H.
options.C: Correct. There are 7 sigma bonds in the main framework including the C-H ends and C-C links, plus 6 sigma bonds from the two CH3 groups, giving 13 sigma bonds in total.
options.D: Too high. 16 is the total number of bonds (sigma + pi). The $\text{C}\equiv\text{C}$ adds 2 pi bonds and the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ adds 1 pi bond, so $13 + 3 = 16$. This option mistakes every pi bond for an extra sigma bond.
